title: OpenAI Chat flow sanitizer and tool invocation normalizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Redwood must accept OpenAI Chat Completions-style requests and produce responses that integrate streaming chunks, function/tool call signals, and Redwood structured outputs without surprising downstream tooling. Existing mappings occasionally create duplicate function-invocation events or emit truncated structured payloads when streaming is interrupted or when both streaming and final payloads arrive separately. Goals: 1) provide a deterministic reconciliation algorithm to merge streamed deltas with the eventual final payload; 2) normalize function/tool invocation shapes into Redwood's canonical 'toolCall' object with stable ids so retries are idempotent; 3) emit intermediate streaming events that are safe for downstream consumers (no half-formed JSON blobs); 4) preserve backwards compatibility for customers relying on legacy OpenAI-shaped payloads.Solution sketch: - Introduce a Flow Sanitizer component in the OpenAI compatibility layer that performs two passes: a streaming framer and a canonicalizer. - Streaming framer: frames incoming stream chunks into tokens and boundaries, attaches a stream-seq header (streamSeq) and a tentative toolCallId when a function signature is detected. The framer will buffer up to a per-request limit (default 2KB) and only emit 'safe' partial text events that are valid UTF-8 and do not break JSON tokens. - Canonicalizer: when a complete function invocation arrives (either as final payload or as an explicit tool call event), the canonicalizer computes a stable toolCallId using HMAC-SHA256 over [request_id, candidate_name, earliest_stream_seq, 8-byte-truncate] and maps OpenAI 'name'/'arguments' shapes to Redwood's toolCall object: {toolCallId, toolName, argsSchemaVersion, rawArgs, parsedArgs, confidenceHints}. All fields are stored as strings in our internal wire format. - Reconciliation algorithm: if a final payload includes a function call that overlaps with previously emitted streamed partials, the canonicalizer will merge as follows: 1) identify partials with matching tentative toolCallId prefix; 2) replay partials to reconstruct best-effort rawArguments; 3) if final rawArguments differs, emit a single 'tool_call/replace' event with both old and new rawValues and a canonical toolCallId; 4) produce a single final structured output event. This avoids duplicate tool invocation side-effects downstream.API contract changes: - No change to public Redwood API surface. The compatibility layer emits internal telemetry fields (streamSeq and tentativeToolCallId) on events for tracing only; these are omitted for public-hosted responses. - Console and observability will receive enriched traces showing mapping decisions.Acceptance criteria: - The compatibility layer must pass the regression test-suite for OpenAI Chat streaming (existing harness) plus three new fuzz cases (see below). - No duplicate tool invocation events observed in 5000 sampled in-prod sessions. - End-to-end latency impact of the sanitizer component under p95 must be <= +4ms for small responses and <= +12ms for long streaming sessions. - Canary rollout shows zero increase in consumer-side parse errors after two days.Edge cases and constraints: - Partial JSON fragments inside streaming chunks must never be emitted as standalone JSON events. We will only emit text deltas; structured tool call emissions are gated until a closing brace is observed or a deterministic timeout (default 2s) elapses. - For very large function arguments streamed across many chunks, the framer will switch to a 'stream-to-tempfile' mode and emit a reference URI rather than inline rawArgs to avoid OOM. - For ambiguous function-call names (multiple tool definitions with same name), canonicalizer uses arg-schema fingerprint to disambiguate; if still ambiguous, it will attach a disambiguation hint and mark customer_impact as 'low' until resolved.Migration plan and rollout: - Phase 1: unit + integration tests, internal dogfood (team chat integrations), feature flag behind 'compat-sanitizer-v1'. - Phase 2: Canary 5% traffic for 48h, composite telemetry checks for duplicate-toolcall, parse-error-rate, and latency. - Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with quick rollback path. Telemetry dashboards and alert runbooks documented in linked design doc.Risks: - Small risk of marginal latency regression on p99 for very high-concurrency hosts; mitigations: micro-optimizations in framer and offload HMAC to async worker. - Risk of mismatch with third-party clients expecting raw OpenAI streaming chunks; mitigation: provide a passthrough configured per-customer and document differences.Test cases to add (fuzz): 1) interleaved tool-call tokens where final braces arrive out-of-order across streams; 2) streaming with intermittent connection resets and replays; 3) function arguments containing large binary-encoded strings that emulate escaped JSON sequences.Each fuzz case must include an expected reconciliation outcome and a golden output for comparison.
implementation_notes: Add HMAC key in config with rotation policy; use KMS-backed key in prod and local key in test harness.
New telemetry metrics: compat.sanitizer.replacements, compat.sanitizer.time_ms, compat.sanitizer.partial_emits
Fallback behavior: if canonicalizer fails, fall back to previous behavior and emit compat.sanitizer.failures metric
Bench harness: extend /infra/loadtests/streaming_compat to simulate 10k concurrent streams
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility layer passes regression suite + 3 new fuzz tests
No duplicate tool invocation events in 5000 sampled sessions
p95 latency increase <= 4ms for small responses; <= 12ms for long streaming sessions
Canary shows no parse error increase after 48h
comments: 2026-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Spiked two approaches for the HMAC recipe; prefer HMAC over random UUIDs for deterministic idempotency across retries.
2026-02-20 - Diego Morales: Implemented streaming framer prototype in Rust; initial microbenchmark shows +1.2ms median overhead.
2026-02-27 - PR #4821: draft implementation submitted (github.com/redwood-inference/compat/pull/4821). Requesting review from @maria (runtime) and @ben (observability).

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Addressed Maria's feedback and added a unit test for surrogate pairs. Added integration test that simulates a reconnect scenario.
2026-03-13 - Product review (Samir Liu): OK to canary behind 'compat-sanitizer-v1' flag. Request to add a dashboard widget for 'tool_call.replace' events.
